title: Assistant Accountant
description:
NXTGEN is working with an established, business to recruit an Assistant Accountant for its finance team. This Assistant Accountant position offers the opportunity to develop your month-end experience within a team where people have progressed.

As Assistant Accountant, you'll work closely with the Management Accountants to prepare monthly management accounts and manufacturer reporting. You'll also work with department managers to investigate discrepancies, answer queries and help them understand the financial performance of their site.

The role combines hands-on accounting with analysis and process improvement, giving you exposure to how finance supports the day-to-day running of a motor retail business.

Key responsibilities as Assistant Accountant
- Support the preparation of monthly management accounts, including accruals and prepayments
- Prepare balance sheet reconciliations, investigate differences and follow up outstanding items
- Assist with monthly manufacturer reporting and process weekly manufacturer bonuses
- Authorise daily payments in line with company procedures
- Monitor outstanding and ageing debt, following up and reporting on overdue balances
- Support vehicle and parts stocktakes, investigate variances and report findings to management
- Respond to management accounts queries and highlight discrepancies or control concerns
- Work with the Management Accountants to identify improvements to financial processes and reporting
- Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation

What we're looking for

You'll have experience within a busy accounts department and be keen to build on your accounting knowledge. AAT Level 3 or an equivalent qualification is preferred, although candidates qualified by experience will also be considered.

Strong numerical skills, attention to detail and confidence using Microsoft packages are essential. You'll be comfortable investigating discrepancies, communicating with colleagues across the business and following queries through to resolution.

Knowledge of Pinnacle DMS would be useful, but isnt essential.

This Assistant Accountant role is based on site in Norwich and would suit someone looking to broaden their experience in management accounts while contributing to an expanding business.

To find out more about this Assistant Accountant opportunity, contact Grace at NXTGEN Recruitment.

title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Credit Controller

description:
Your new company
Are you an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys building strong customer relationships while delivering excellent cash collection results? This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing and successful organisation where your communication skills, commercial awareness, and ability to resolve outstanding debt will directly contribute to business performance and customer satisfaction.

Our client is a well-established and growing business with a strong reputation for customer service and operational excellence. They are committed to investing in their people, supporting career development, and creating a positive and collaborative working environment. As part of a successful credit control finance team, you will play a key role in managing customer accounts, maintaining strong client relationships, and ensuring the timely collection of outstanding debt.

Your new roleReporting to the Credit Manager, you will take ownership of a ledger of customer accounts, proactively managing collection activities while delivering a professional and customer-focused service. Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining a portfolio of customer accounts.
- Chasing outstanding debt through telephone, email, and written correspondence.
- Building strong relationships with customers to encourage prompt payment.
- Negotiating payment plans and resolving account queries.
- Monitoring aged debt and reducing overdue balances.
- Investigating and resolving invoice and payment disputes.
- Allocating cash and reconciling customer accounts.
- Producing aged debt and collection reports.
- Supporting credit risk management activities.
- Working closely with internal departments to ensure excellent customer outcomes

What you'll need to succeed
You will bring previous Credit Control or Accounts Receivable experience, alongside a proven track record of confident credit collections and debt recovery. You will also possess strong customer relationship management skills, excellent communication and negotiation abilities, with the confidence to hold professional conversations regarding outstanding balances.

In addition, you will demonstrate excellent organisational and problem-solving capabilities, strong attention to detail and accuracy, experience using finance systems and Microsoft Excel, and a proactive, resilient approach with the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities effectively.

- Coordinate travel arrangements for site personnel and visitors together with the home-office Business Mobility Coordinators, Travel Coordinators and Project Construction and Commissioning Managers.

description:

This is a great opportunity for someone with Purchase Ledger or Accounts Payable experience who is looking for a varied role offering responsibility for their own supplier accounts and exposure to wider finance processes.

You'll work closely with colleagues across finance, purchasing and operational teams, combining day-to-day invoice processing with reconciliations, subcontractor payments and query resolution.

What You'll Be Doing
- Processing supplier invoices and credit notes.
- Matching invoices against purchase orders and goods received.
- Coding costs accurately to contracts and relevant cost codes.
- Managing your own portfolio of supplier accounts.
- Completing supplier statement reconciliations and investigating discrepancies.
- Resolving invoice and payment queries with suppliers and internal teams.
- Reviewing and processing subcontractor payment information.
- Preparing subcontractor payment runs.
- Ensuring invoices and payments meet internal controls and procedures.
- Supporting the wider finance team when required.

What We're Looking For

You'll already have experience within Purchase Ledger, Accounts Payable or a similar finance role and be comfortable working in a busy environment.

Ideally, you'll have:
- Good experience processing invoices and reconciling supplier accounts.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- The ability to organise and prioritise your own workload.
- Confidence investigating discrepancies and resolving queries.
- Good communication skills when dealing with suppliers and colleagues.
- Competence with Excel and accounting systems.
- A proactive approach and the ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Knowledge of CIS, VAT or subcontractor payments would be advantageous, as would experience within construction or another project-led environment.

What's on Offer?

A varied Finance Assistant position within a friendly and experienced team, offering the opportunity to take ownership of your workload and broaden your accounts experience.

Please apply online or contact Justin Murray at Big Sky Additions for a confidential chat.

title: Assistant Accountant with Bookkeeping; independent, innovative, collaborative practice
description:
Our client is an independent reputable accountancy firm servicing the Norfolk region for well over a decade. They offer a personal, collaborative and supportive working environment where their staff are treated as equals and not as commodities.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented experienced individual from practice to join the team to undertake Assistant Accountant and Bookkeeping responsibilities.

The successful candidate will be involved in bookkeeping, year-end accounts preparation, VAT returns, and general client accounting support, working closely with a range of owner-managed businesses and SMEs.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintaining accurate bookkeeping records for a portfolio of clients.
- Preparing VAT returns
- Assisting with and preparing year-end accounts up to trial balance and final accounts stage.
- Liaising directly with clients to resolve accounting queries.
- Processing bank reconciliations, journals, accruals, and prepayments.
- Supporting senior team members with accounts preparation and client work.
- Ensuring work is completed accurately and within agreed deadlines.
- Working with cloud accounting software to support clients and maintain financial records.

This is an ideal post for an experienced practice-based Bookkeeper or Accounts Assistant who is looking to be a key team member - not just another number - and truly add value to clients in an established and forward-thinking accountancy firm.

About You: To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous experience working within an accountancy practice environment - essential
- AAT Level 3 or Level 4 qualification.
- Experience preparing a full set of accounts for a variety of clients.
- Solid bookkeeping skills and a strong understanding of accounting principles.
- Experience working with clients across a range of sectors and industries.
- Proficiency with Xero, Iris and QuickBooks.
- Strong communication and organisational skills.
- A high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- The ability to manage multiple client deadlines effectively.

What's on Offer
- Varied and interesting client portfolio.
- Exposure to businesses across multiple industries.
- Ongoing professional development and training.
- Supportive and collaborative team environment.

Apply now or contact Natalie Harden at Reed for an initial discussion to learn more.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
This position has now been filled. If you are interested in this type of vacancy moving forward, please do send your CV across for the future

This is a great opportunity to join a well-established, family-run business that is continuing to grow. The role is hands-on, tasked with supporting the day-to-day financial operations of the business and working alongside the existing accounts function.

As a key team member, you'll be responsible for keeping the financial side of the business running smoothly - using your proven accounts experience to provide integral support within the finance and administration operations, showcasing your practical and proactive approach to work.

This opportunity is based a few miles outside of Great Yarmouth and due to the remote location, a driving license and vehicle is essential.

Salary is offered at £30,000 with the role being considered both full-time or part-time at a minimum of 30 hours per week.

Benefits
- Flexible working considered
- Opportunity to work from home once established in the role
- 3 days' annual leave used for the Christmas/New Year shutdown
- Holiday entitlement increases after 2 years, from 20 up to 25 days
- Stakeholder pension scheme
- Free parking
- Bi-annual company socials
- Corporate workwear if required
- A friendly, family-run working environment with a genuinely non-hierarchical culture

The Company

Working across sectors including healthcare, education and national infrastructure, this business provides a specialist service to clients across the UK and parts of Europe.

The company has a close-knit, down-to-earth culture, with strong team morale and a genuine willingness to all muck in and get things done. As the business continues to scale, this is an excellent opportunity to become apart of the growth and join a business where everyone really does play their part.

The Day to Day
- Recording and maintaining accurate financial transactions and records
- Processing supplier invoices and making payments
- Raising customer invoices and uploading invoices to relevant portals
- Reconciling supplier statements and bank accounts
- Monitoring aged debtors and highlighting outstanding payments
- Maintaining and reviewing sales and purchase ledgers
- Supporting payroll preparation, including expenses and relevant payroll data
- Assisting with VAT returns and other financial reporting
- Supporting the preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial information
- Providing financial information for management review
- Identifying and highlighting discrepancies and helping to resolve them
- Supporting internal and external audits and maintaining compliance with financial procedures

You Will Have / Be
- Previous experience in a similar accounts-based role with understanding of accounting principles
- Experience using accounting software such as Sage or Xero
- Good understanding of sales and purchase ledgers
- Experience with reconciliations and balancing accounts
- Awareness of aged debtors and the importance of timely payment
- A baseline understanding of P&L
- Good attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise your workload
- Happy to speak to customers and suppliers regarding accounts queries when required
- A proactive, self-motivated and flexible approach

An accountancy qualification would be useful but isn't essential. What matters most is that you understand the fundamentals of accounts and have the practical experience to get on with the job.

How to Apply

To hear more details about this opportunity, please email your CV to Ruth Harding - Business Partner at R13 Recruitment. If you do not hear from us within 5 working days of submitting your CV, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion

title: Receptionist
company: Southgates Medical Centre & The Woottons Surgery
advertiser_name: Southgates Medical Centre & The Woottons Surgery
location: King's Lynn, PE30 5QX, King's Lynn, PE30 3PT
description: Southgates and The Woottons Surgeries are based in King's Lynn and we have a long and proud history of excellent patient care. We are looking for a Receptionist to join our friendly and professional team. These are permanent hours of 27.50 hours per week. The hours are: Monday 08:00-18:30 Tuesday 08:00-13:00 Wednesday 08:00-13:00 Friday 08:00-17:00 The successful candidate will demonstrate excellent interpersonal and organisational skills as well as a level of competency in IT. Ideally you will be a team player who is adaptable and can demonstrate outstanding communication skills, motivation, initiative and a willingness to learn. We are seeking a candidate with ideally at least 3 GCSEs grade A-C, one of which to be English. Job Summary: Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Job Responsibilities: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. When necessary, enter requests for home visits onto the computer, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non NHS) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Monitor and complete clinical system tasks as required by the Reception Supervisor, Practice Manager and GPs. Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Reception Supervisor or the Practice Manager. Attend team and practice meetings. Give results and/or information to the patient as directed by the doctors. Accept and ensure all specimens are clearly labelled and pass on to Healthcare staff for appropriate recording prior to collection by hospital transport. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified to the Health and Safety Team immediately. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Attending all training courses and sessions deemed as mandatory by the Practice Manager. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Participate in audit where appropriate.
